newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end firmer on late buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end firmer on late buying.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks ended firmer on late buying, but secondary stocks stayed in negative territory throughout the day, dealers said.
Trading volume was thin as there was no fresh leads to lift market sentiment, they said.
"It was a very slow day. The market looks like it's in a holiday mood," said a dealer at SJ Securities. "The market has gone into a lethargic state and needs something significant to bring it up."
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 8.85 points or 0.74 percent at 1,197.30.
The Second Board index fell 8.12 points or 1.49 percent to 536.94.
Dealers said many players were waiting for the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.
But they added that following the recent falls in Malaysian stocks, they have not ruled out the possibilty of some year-end window dressing.
Telekom Malaysia and Malayan Banking led the rise in heavyweight stocks, up 50 cents each. Tenaga Nasional, Resorts World and Sime Darby gained between 10 and 30 cents each.
